record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.context_brief: Ugly and bad theories as affine Grassmannian slices
record.original_question: Affine Grassmannian slices appear as Coulomb branches of framed quivers. Can one study the Coulomb branches of “ugly” and “bad” theories, in the sense of Gaiotto and Witten, as generalized affine Grassmannian slices?

evidence.quote: Question 9. Study the Coulomb branch for “ugly” and “bad” theories (in the sense of [54]) as (generalized) affine Grassmannian slices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. To a 3-dimensional N=4 gauge theory determined by a complex reductive group G and a quaternionic representation N, Braverman–Finkelberg–Nakajima associate a Coulomb branch M_C(G,N), a (typically singular) affine symplectic variety. When the data come from a framed quiver of finite ADE type — i.e. G = ∏ GL(v_i) and N is built from the quiver arrows together with framing maps determined by dimension vectors v = (v_i) and w = (w_i) — the Coulomb branch is known to be isomorphic to a (generalized) affine Grassmannian slice attached to the corresponding pair of dominant coweights determined by w and w − Cv (where C is the Cartan matrix), provided the quiver gauge theory is "good" in the following sense of Gaiotto–Witten:

For each node i of the quiver, set
   d_i := (the number of fundamental hypermultiplets at node i) − 2·(rank at node i) + (contributions from neighbouring nodes)
       = w_i + ∑_{j∼i} v_j − 2 v_i.
The theory is called
 • good if d_i ≥ 1 for every node i,
 • ugly if d_i ≥ 0 for every node i and d_i = 0 for at least one node,
 • bad if d_i < 0 for some node i.

Equivalently in highest-weight language, with λ = ∑ w_i ω_i and μ = λ − ∑ v_i α_i, the theory is good when λ − μ is a positive sum of simple roots and μ is dominant (and "deep enough"), ugly when μ lies on a wall in a specified sense, and bad otherwise.

Problem. For framed quiver gauge theories that are ugly or bad in the above sense, give a description of the Coulomb branch M_C(G,N) as a generalized affine Grassmannian slice (or a suitable extension of that notion). More precisely:

 (i) For ugly theories, identify M_C(G,N) with a generalized slice W^{λ}_{μ} (or a related variety, e.g. a slice for a smaller group or with shifted parameters) and describe the associated geometric structures (symplectic resolution, Poisson deformation, quantization by a truncated shifted Yangian).

 (ii) For bad theories, where μ fails to be dominant and standard Gaiotto–Witten predictions break down, develop a generalized notion of affine Grassmannian slice — for instance, slices in the affine Grassmannian for shifted Yangians with arbitrary (not necessarily dominant) shift, or geometric objects naturally attached to non-dominant μ — and prove that M_C(G,N) is isomorphic to such an object, including matching of Poisson structure and quantization.

Provide a uniform construction covering both ugly and bad cases.
artifact.category_tag: Coulomb branches and affine Grassmannian slices
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up the foundational work of Braverman–Finkelberg–Nakajima identifying Coulomb branches of good/ugly framed ADE quiver gauge theories with (generalized) affine Grassmannian slices, plus follow-ups on shifted Yangians, Hamiltonian reduction, symplectic leaves, and Kac-Moody slices via fundamental monopole operators (through 2024). However, no paper found gives a uniform description of the Coulomb branches of ugly and especially bad theories as generalized affine Grassmannian slices in full generality; the question appears to remain open, with only partial results in special cases.

status_evidence.title: Coulomb branches of 3d N=4 quiver gauge theories and slices in the affine Grassmannian
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies Coulomb branches of framed ADE quiver gauge theories with (generalized) affine Grassmannian slices in good cases.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework but does not resolve the ugly/bad cases uniformly.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian reduction for affine Grassmannian slices and truncated shifted Yangians
status_evidence.snippet: Develops generalized slices and shifted Yangians for non-dominant shifts.
status_evidence.claim: Provides tools potentially relevant to bad theories but does not complete the identification.

status_evidence.title: Fundamental Monopole Operators and Embeddings of Kac-Moody Affine Grassmannian Slices
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work on Kac-Moody slices as Coulomb branches.
status_evidence.claim: Extends the dictionary but the ugly/bad classification problem remains unaddressed in full generality.
